finding: The always-available possibility-conditioned preprocessor now has synthetic component evidence: required-evidence recall 1.00 and top-1 intended affordance 1.00 versus 0.8833 and 0.30 for flat lexical retrieval on a 10-query/400-distractor fixture. It remains non-authoritative context and is not yet a validated FRANK default read path.
counterhypotheses: Synthetic benchmark design may favor the mechanism.
Always-on preprocessing can add latency or omit rare decisive evidence on real FRANK traces.
Downstream 4B outcome may not track claim-retrieval metrics.
next_gate: Matched H1/real-snapshot traces comparing always-on preprocessor, model-triggered retrieval, FTS5/BM25, dense/hybrid, and raw/full-state baselines under equal context budgets with outcome, counterevidence, re-expansion, latency and token/KV metrics.
identity_boundary: Research Entity != Frank; candidate rank/activation does not mint Frank authority.
target_scope: Final acceptance remains Andreas Ubuntu only.
